subject: future
topic: AI can read some medical scans as well as specialists
angle: While deep learning systems can match or exceed human performance in specific diagnostic tasks, the evidence is undermined by high rates of bias, inconsistent reporting, and methodological variations.
title: The truth about ai diagnostics

hooks.text: Can ai read your scans better than a doctor?
Ai matches human skill, but the data is flawed.
You trust the machine more than the evidence.
A blue screen flickers in a silent clinic.
99% of studies show high risk of bias.

reveal.headline: 99% of studies have high risk of bias.
reveal.body: The evidence on ai diagnostic accuracy is frequently compromised by poor study quality and lack of external validation.

explain.headline: Ai matches human performance in some tasks.
explain.body: Deep learning models have diagnostic performance equivalent to healthcare professionals. However, variation in methodology and terminology can lead to an overestimation of their accuracy.

matters.headline: The data is not settled.
matters.body: That may be why claims about ai replacing specialists remain contested. While it performs well in specific areas, the underlying evidence is often inconsistent.

example.headline: A scan sits in a dark room.
example.body: You wait for a result. A machine processes the pixels. A human looks for a fracture. The line between them blurs.

claims.text: In a review of 2976 studies, 99% of studies identified for inclusion had at least one area at high or unclear risk of bias or applicability concerns.

claims.text: Extensive variation in methodology, terminology and outcome measures in deep learning studies can lead to an overestimation of the diagnostic accuracy of DL algorithms on medical imaging.
claims.quote: Heterogeneity was high between studies and extensive variation in methodology, terminology and outcome measures was noted. This can lead to an overestimation of the diagnostic accuracy of DL algorithms on medical imaging.

claims.text: Deep learning models have diagnostic performance that is equivalent to that of health-care professionals.
claims.quote: Our review found the diagnostic performance of deep learning models to be equivalent to that of health-care professionals.

claims.text: Radiologists were more specific than AI overall and in several subgroups, and were more sensitive to hip fractures before FDR correction.
claims.quote: Radiologists, on the other hand, were more specific than AI overall and in several subgroups, and more sensitive to hip fractures before FDR correction.

verdict: The evidence shows that AI can perform as well as specialists in some areas, but the reliability of these claims is frequently compromised by poor study quality and lack of external validation.
caveat: A significant majority of studies identified in these reviews showed at least one area of high or unclear risk of bias or applicability concerns.
caption:
Ai can perform as well as healthcare professionals in specific diagnostic tasks. 

Research shows that while deep learning matches human performance, 99% of studies identified in reviews showed at least one area of high or unclear risk of bias. 

How much do you trust a diagnosis made by a black box?
